dedupe_keys.name: fmlist and fmscan worldwide database of fm dab tv and mw transmitters

description: FMLIST is a volunteer-run database of broadcast radio and television transmitters around the world, started in print in 1986 by the German radio enthusiast Günter Lorenz and online since 2005 at fmlist.org, with its sister site fmscan.org, run by the association UKW/TV-Arbeitskreis. It describes itself as the most complete database of FM, DAB and TV stations worldwide, with MWLIST covering medium wave. Editors from the DX community, who listen for distant stations, and contributions from users compile each station's frequency, programme, transmitter site with coordinates, power, antenna height and polarisation, RDS and digital identifiers, and links to websites and live streams, and logs of receptions. FMSCAN offers maps of transmitters and reception predictions for any location. Since 2023 FMLIST and MWLIST are the main source for the World Radio TV Handbook. The project is non-commercial and open for anyone to contribute and use; full access to the FMLIST database requires a free login. Coverage: worldwide, strongest in Europe. Format and access: web database with login, maps and exports for registered users, free; no formal open licence was found. Caveats: accuracy depends on volunteers; official regulator databases are more authoritative where they exist. Simulation uses: locations and technical parameters of broadcast transmitters in countries without open regulator data, for coverage and hazard exposure models. Related records: the Ofcom, ISED, ANFR and FCC databases are official national sources.
